questions.questionTextEn: Was the eye exposed to a chemical, acid, cleaning product, or unknown liquid?
questions.rationaleEn: Begin immediate continuous irrigation and obtain emergency in-person assessment; the source-only chemical-eye family is not generated.

questions.questionTextEn: After emergency features are excluded, are itchy or watery eyes still presumed to be allergy without an in-person examination?

questions.questionTextEn: Is this a baby with red, sticky eyes, does the caller wear contact lenses with eyelid spots, or have symptoms not cleared within 7 days?
questions.rationaleEn: NHS.UK guidance recommends a primary-care review for these situations.

careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar 999 for major trauma, collapse or severe systemic deterioration; otherwise proceed immediately to the locally approved emergency eye destination. Call Back If: vision worsens; pain, vomiting or confusion increases.

Stop wearing contact lenses until clinically cleared. Call Back If: symptoms worsen; pain, light sensitivity or vision change develops.

Call Back If: pain, light sensitivity or vision change; swelling, fever or systemic allergy develops.

protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: UAT-only assessment of a transient loss of consciousness or suspected faint in an adult or child, including pregnancy-related, cardiac, neurologic, bleeding, and injury risks; not approved for real-patient or production use. Adult patient. Female.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: Is the patient fully responsive and breathing normally now? Gasping or irregular breathing is not normal.
What is the patient's exact age, when did the episode occur, how long did unresponsiveness last, and have they completely returned to their usual behavior, speech, and movement?
What posture and activity preceded the episode, were there warning symptoms, and what did a witness observe during and after it?
Is there chest pain, palpitations, breathlessness, severe headache, new weakness or speech change, significant bleeding, black stool, vomiting blood, seizure features, or serious injury?
Is the patient pregnant or recently pregnant, or could pregnancy be possible; and is there abdominal or one-sided pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, or shoulder-tip pain?

protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: UAT-only assessment of flank, side, or back pain where renal stone, infection, urinary obstruction, vascular emergency, pregnancy complication, or another cause must be considered; not approved for real-patient or production use. Adult patient. Female.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What is the patient's exact age, where is the pain, when did it start, was onset sudden, and does it travel to the abdomen, groin, shoulder, or testicle?
Is the patient confused, difficult to wake, fainting or collapsed, severely short of breath, cold or clammy, or rapidly worsening?
Is there fever, shaking chills, vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, painful urination, foul or cloudy urine, blood in urine, or inability to pass urine?
Is the patient pregnant, recently pregnant, or possibly pregnant, and is there one-sided pelvic or abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, fainting, or reduced fetal movement?

Is there a known abdominal aortic aneurysm, solitary kidney, kidney transplant, significant kidney disease, urinary abnormality, diabetes, immune suppression, recent urinary procedure, or anticoagulant use?
Is the patient a child, unable to communicate symptoms reliably, or experiencing a first episode that has not been assessed in person?

questions.questionTextEn: Is there collapse, confusion, reduced responsiveness, severe breathing difficulty, cold or clammy skin, or rapid deterioration; sudden severe abdominal, back, or flank pain especially with a known aneurysm or pulsating abdominal mass; complete inability to pass urine with severe pain or illness; or pregnancy/possible pregnancy with severe one-sided abdominal or pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, fainting, or collapse?
questions.rationaleEn: These features may indicate shock, ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, complete urinary obstruction, or ruptured ectopic pregnancy. NHS identifies sudden severe abdominal or back pain as an AAA emergency, and RCOG identifies severe pain or collapse as possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

questions.questionTextEn: After immediate emergency features are excluded, is there fever or shaking chills, feeling very unwell, severe or uncontrolled pain, vomiting or dehydration, blood in urine, painful or foul-smelling urine, reduced urine, inability to pass urine, a solitary or transplanted kidney, significant renal or urinary disease, diabetes or immune suppression; or is the patient pregnant, recently pregnant, or a child?
questions.rationaleEn: An infected obstructed kidney and sepsis require urgent hospital care. NICE recommends hospital or specialist assessment when pyelonephritis is accompanied by serious illness, pregnancy, dehydration, structural urinary abnormality, diabetes, immune suppression, or pediatric age.

questions.questionTextEn: With all emergency and higher-risk features excluded, is this new or recurrent flank pain that has not yet been assessed in person during this episode?
questions.rationaleEn: A kidney stone cannot be confirmed by telephone. Flank pain may require examination, urinalysis, renal function and infection tests, pregnancy testing where relevant, and age- and pregnancy-appropriate imaging before home management is judged safe.

careAdvice.titleEn: Emergency flank or back pain — call Qatar 999
careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Call Qatar 999 immediately and follow the operator's instructions. Keep the patient resting in the safest comfortable position, observed, and warm. If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start age-appropriate CPR as directed. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care. Call Back If: collapse or reduced responsiveness; worsening pain, bleeding, breathing difficulty, or shock.

careAdvice.titleEn: High-risk flank pain — same-day hospital assessment

Call Back If: pain worsens or becomes sudden and severe; fever, vomiting, bleeding, reduced urine, fainting, or pregnancy-related symptoms.

If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start age-appropriate CPR as directed. Call Qatar 999 now, follow the call-taker's ambulance and emergency-transport instructions, and do not self-drive. Do not delay emergency care. Call Back If: collapse or reduced responsiveness; worsening pain, bleeding, breathing difficulty, or shock.

careAdvice.titleEn: High-risk flank pain — same-day hospital assessment
careAdvice.instructionTextEn: Arrange immediate same-day in-person assessment through the Qatar hospital or maternity destination approved for this UAT environment. Do not delay for a teleconsult. The patient may need urine and blood tests, renal-function and infection assessment, and imaging. Do not use leftover antibiotics or start, stop, or change medicine. A clinician or pharmacist must select analgesia after considering age, pregnancy, kidney function, allergy, bleeding risk, other medicines, and dehydration. Do not force fluids if the patient is vomiting, unable to urinate, or may have obstruction. Call Back If: fever, shaking, confusion, or worsening illness; inability to urinate; increasing pain, vomiting, bleeding, or fainting.

Arrange prompt same-day in-person assessment using the Qatar route approved for this UAT environment. A clinician may need urinalysis, blood tests, pregnancy testing where relevant, and imaging; suspected renal colic in pregnancy generally requires ultrasound rather than CT as the initial imaging approach. Until assessed, use only medicine already confirmed as appropriate for this patient and do not assume the pain is a kidney stone or force excessive fluid intake. Call Back If: pain worsens or becomes sudden and severe; fever, vomiting, bleeding, reduced urine, fainting, or pregnancy-related symptoms.

protocols.clinicalDefinitionEn: UAT-only assessment of flank, side, or back pain where renal stone, infection, urinary obstruction, vascular emergency, pregnancy complication, or another cause must be considered; not approved for real-patient or production use. Child patient. Male.

initialAssessmentQuestions.promptTextEn: What is the patient's exact age, where is the pain, when did it start, was onset sudden, and does it travel to the abdomen, groin, shoulder, or testicle?
Is the patient confused, difficult to wake, fainting or collapsed, severely short of breath, cold or clammy, or rapidly worsening?
Is there fever, shaking chills, vomiting, inability to keep fluids down, painful urination, foul or cloudy urine, blood in urine, or inability to pass urine?
Is the patient pregnant, recently pregnant, or possibly pregnant, and is there one-sided pelvic or abdominal pain, vaginal bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, fainting, or reduced fetal movement?

Is there a known abdominal aortic aneurysm, solitary kidney, kidney transplant, significant kidney disease, urinary abnormality, diabetes, immune suppression, recent urinary procedure, or anticoagulant use?
Is the patient a child, unable to communicate symptoms reliably, or experiencing a first episode that has not been assessed in person?
What has a safe parent or caregiver observed about alertness, breathing, pain, swelling, fever, eating or drinking, sleep, play, and normal activity?

questions.questionTextEn: Is there collapse, confusion, reduced responsiveness, severe breathing difficulty, cold or clammy skin, or rapid deterioration; sudden severe abdominal, back, or flank pain especially with a known aneurysm or pulsating abdominal mass; complete inability to pass urine with severe pain or illness; or pregnancy/possible pregnancy with severe one-sided abdominal or pelvic pain, vaginal bleeding, shoulder-tip pain, fainting, or collapse?
questions.rationaleEn: These features may indicate shock, ruptured abdominal aortic aneurysm, complete urinary obstruction, or ruptured ectopic pregnancy. NHS identifies sudden severe abdominal or back pain as an AAA emergency, and RCOG identifies severe pain or collapse as possible ruptured ectopic pregnancy.

questions.questionTextEn: After immediate emergency features are excluded, is there fever or shaking chills, feeling very unwell, severe or uncontrolled pain, vomiting or dehydration, blood in urine, painful or foul-smelling urine, reduced urine, inability to pass urine, a solitary or transplanted kidney, significant renal or urinary disease, diabetes or immune suppression; or is the patient pregnant, recently pregnant, or a child?
questions.rationaleEn: An infected obstructed kidney and sepsis require urgent hospital care. NICE recommends hospital or specialist assessment when pyelonephritis is accompanied by serious illness, pregnancy, dehydration, structural urinary abnormality, diabetes, immune suppression, or pediatric age.

questions.questionTextEn: With all emergency and higher-risk features excluded, is this new or recurrent flank pain that has not yet been assessed in person during this episode?
questions.rationaleEn: A kidney stone cannot be confirmed by telephone. Flank pain may require examination, urinalysis, renal function and infection tests, pregnancy testing where relevant, and age- and pregnancy-appropriate imaging before home management is judged safe.
